Habermas's "law as medium" means law as a steering medium that coordinates the economic and administrative systems through sanctions and incentives, and "law as institution" means a normative order whose validity rests on discursive legitimation. The shared note's candidates don't match this: Habermas's "medium" is not mass media, and his "institution" is not a concrete body like the courts. I still can't identify the right option because the statements were never pasted, so please share them and I'll match one.
